title: Sponsorship in numbers
heading: How far off is your gut?
intro: Eight real numbers about what brands pay to be part of sport, music and big events, and what they get for it.
Every figure is real and sourced. Bet on how sure you are, not just on what you think.

outro.heading: Every deal is a trade.
paras: Sponsors buy attention, trust and access; the people and events they sponsor get money and reach. The prices are rarely what people guess, and nor are the side effects.
Today, ask what each side really wants from a deal before you judge the price.

questions.q: Slazenger supplies the tennis balls for Wimbledon. Since when?
questions.sub: one of the longest partnerships in sport
questions.explain: Since 1902, when leading players asked for its balls; Slazenger calls it the longest partnership in sporting goods history. The balls have only been yellow, rather than white, since 1986.
questions.source: Slazenger Heritage, Wimbledon tennis balls; The All England Club

questions.q: Coca-Cola is one of the Olympic Games' top worldwide sponsors. Since which Games has it been involved?
questions.explain: Since Amsterdam 1928, when it shipped 1,000 cases of Coke with the US team. In 2019 it extended its deal to 2032, jointly with China's Mengniu Dairy, in a package reported at about $3 billion.
questions.source: IOC / The Coca-Cola Company; Fox Business and Al Jazeera, June 2019

questions.q: In 2021 the Staples Center in Los Angeles, home of the Lakers, was renamed Crypto.com Arena. What was the 20-year naming deal reportedly worth?
questions.explain: About $700 million, one of the biggest arena naming deals ever, signed at the height of the crypto boom. The crypto market crashed the following year; the name stayed.

questions.q: Apple Music reportedly pays the NFL about $50 million a year to sponsor the Super Bowl half-time show. What does the headline performer get paid?
questions.explain: Only the union minimum, roughly $1,000 a day. The league covers production costs, but the stars come for the audience: more than 100 million viewers, and a jump in streams the week after.

questions.q: Berlin's big arena near Ostbahnhof opened in 2008 as the O2 World and later became the Mercedes-Benz Arena. What has it been called since 2024?
questions.sub: and the Uber Eats Music Hall next door
questions.explain: Uber Arena. The owner, AEG, called the deal the largest naming-rights partnership in Germany; the music hall next door became the Uber Eats Music Hall.

questions.q: At the 2010 World Cup a Dutch beer brand that was not an official sponsor dressed fans in orange mini-dresses at a match. How many women in the group did officials detain?
questions.explain: Thirty-six. FIFA called it ambush marketing, and two of the women were arrested as alleged organisers (the charges were dropped after a settlement with FIFA). The story went round the world, giving the brand far more coverage than the dresses alone.

questions.q: In 2024 Formula 1 signed a ten-year global partnership with the luxury group LVMH (Louis Vuitton, Moët Hennessy, TAG Heuer). What was it reported to be worth each year?
questions.explain: More than $100 million a year, about $1 billion over ten years, according to Bloomberg's sources; neither side published the figure. It replaced Rolex, which had sponsored F1 since 2013.

questions.q: Front-of-shirt gambling sponsors are banned in the Premier League from 2026-27. In 2025-26, the last season they were allowed, how many of the 20 clubs had one?
questions.explain: Eleven, the same number as the season before, as clubs signed a last round of deals before the ban. Gambling brands can still appear on sleeves and on boards around the pitch.
